subthemes.name: Learning from unlabeled data without labels
subthemes.gist: Papers use contrastive learning and self-supervised methods to train models on large unlabeled datasets by predicting parts of the data from other parts, avoiding the need for expensive manual labels.

subthemes.name: Understanding what neural networks actually learn
subthemes.gist: Papers analyze and measure the geometry of learned representations to understand how networks encode information, what patterns they capture, and whether they learn interpretable structure.

subthemes.name: Bridging different types of data together
subthemes.gist: Papers connect vision and language, audio and text, and multiple views of the same object by learning representations that make different data types comparable and usable together.

subthemes.name: Keeping knowledge as data changes over time
subthemes.gist: Papers tackle continual learning and domain adaptation by building models that learn from new data without forgetting old knowledge, important for real-world systems that must evolve.

subthemes.name: Grouping similar things without being told how
subthemes.gist: Papers use clustering and prototype learning to organize data into meaningful groups by discovering natural patterns, without relying on human-provided category labels.

subthemes.name: Distilling and transferring what models learn
subthemes.gist: Papers compress large pretrained models and transfer their knowledge to new domains through knowledge distillation and diffusion models, making powerful representations accessible on limited devices.

subthemes.name: Making models work with partial or noisy information
subthemes.gist: Papers handle incomplete multi-view data, noisy labels, and uncertain signals by using mathematical frameworks like optimal transport and information theory to extract reliable patterns.

subthemes.name: Geometry and structure in representation spaces
subthemes.gist: Papers exploit geometric properties like symmetries and manifold structures to build better models, using techniques like hyperbolic space and polar embeddings to capture hierarchical relationships.

subthemes.name: Specialized models for specialized tasks
subthemes.gist: Papers use techniques like federated learning and mixture of experts to build systems where different parts of the model specialize in different tasks or data sources, improving efficiency and performance.

subthemes.name: Deeper theory for better representations
subthemes.gist: Papers provide mathematical foundations using variational inference, Riemannian geometry, and information theory to understand why certain representation learning methods work and how to improve them.
